program_note:
“Double Vision” is a condition in which a person sees two images of a single object; “Double Double Vision” is thus four images of a single object.  The quadruple images of the harp in this composition are not merely repeated images, however, but images that are subtly changed or altered over time.  Thus chords echo and sink down in pitch, melodies echo and anticipate themselves, and short individual melodies combine to produce long melodic lines in ways that could never be achieved with a single harp.  Over the course of the composition, these echoes and repetitions combine to increase the energy and widen the sonic space of the opening material, which returns (as one final echo — one final doubled vision) at the end.

-David S. Lefkowitz

Los Angeles, June, 2018
